summary: trips.list and trips.get moved off both public REST travel APIs (Itinerary v4, Trip v1.1 -- see trips-legacy-api-and-auth-gate.json, now superseded) onto the internal GraphQL BFF the Concur Trips UI itself uses (POST https://www-us2.api.concursolutions.com/cds/graphql, operations loadTripList and a hand-constructed tripDetail query against TravelTripQuery.trip(id)). This is CONFIRMED WORKING under the same cookie-session auth already used for reports/expenses -- no OAuth2 needed, resolving what trips-legacy-api-and-auth-gate.json had concluded was a hard auth-model boundary. A regen must not revert to either REST API; both are dead ends regardless of path correctness.
reason: User asked to specifically test flights and hotels under Travel. Both REST APIs (Itinerary v4 and Trip v1.1) were re-confirmed to require a genuine OAuth2 access token via direct 401s. Per the user's direction to 'use the UI instead', the actual Trips UI (us2.concursolutions.com/travel/trip/list) was driven via agent-browser (--profile Default --headed, user completed Okta SSO manually) and its real network traffic captured via agent-browser's native `network har`/`network requests` commands -- no browser screenshots at any point, consistent with the session's hard no-screenshots constraint. The list page's actual data call was `loadTripList`, a GraphQL query against /cds/graphql, captured verbatim including query text and variables. Full-schema GraphQL introspection (`{__schema{...}}`) is disabled server-side (403), but single-type introspection (`{__type(name:...)}`) is NOT -- this allowed walking the schema (TravelQuery -> TravelTripQuery -> TravelTrip -> TravelTripBooking -> TravelAirBooking/TravelAirBookingJourney/TravelTripHotelBooking/TravelTripHotelBookingData) to construct and live-validate a `tripDetail` query for trip detail, confirmed by getting a clean domain-level 'ID malformed' response (not an auth or parse error) for a placeholder ID. The account under test has zero real Travel-module bookings (confirmed via both the home page 'No Trips' widget and the Trip List page with all status filters enabled), so the tripDetail query's field selection could not be validated against real flight/hotel data in this session -- only against the schema and a placeholder ID.

changes.description: Fully rewritten as a hand-authored file (dropped the 'Generated by...DO NOT EDIT' header, following the same convention as forkable-pp-cli's forkable_gql.go for GraphQL-backed CLIs). Defines concurGraphQLPath and gqlErrorEntry (shared with trips_get.go), the loadTripList query captured verbatim from live traffic, and a manual nextToken pagination loop for --all. Dropped --user-id (the real query has no per-user lookup variable; it is always scoped to the session's own user). Added --past/--upcoming flags matching the UI's actual filter.quick values.

Fully rewritten as a hand-authored file. Defines the tripDetail query (constructed via live introspection, not captured -- no real trip existed to click into) reaching TravelTripQuery.trip(id), covering air/journeys and hotel/bookingData fields. Returns notFoundErr for a null trip result.

Guard-clause comment and message corrected: trips no longer requires OAuth2 (that finding applied only to the abandoned REST APIs), so this command is now blocked solely by the still-unresolved available_expenses gap, not a compound trips+available_expenses gap. NOTE: the --dry-run preview path (the tripPath variable a few lines below the guard) still references the abandoned Trip v1.1 REST URL and was not updated to preview the real GraphQL call -- this command is still fully blocked in live mode regardless, so the inaccuracy is cosmetic (dry-run preview only), but a future pass should either share trips_get.go's query construction or drop the stale preview path.
Same guard-message correction as trips_reconcile.go, same known dry-run preview cosmetic gap.

Removed 'trips' from resourceReadPaths, resourceDetailPaths, and resourceReadConfigs entirely -- those maps back the generic GET path+params helpers (resolveReadWithStrategyAndResponsePath, resolvePaginatedReadWithStrategy), which trips.list/trips.get no longer use (they call c.PostQueryWithParams directly with a GraphQL body). Leaving stale entries would mislead any other caller resolving 'trips' generically.

Removed 'trips' from syncResourcePath's map for the same reason -- the generic sync interface is GET-only and cannot drive a POST GraphQL body. `sync trips` / `sync --resources trips` now fails with a clean 'unknown sync resource' error instead of attempting a broken GET.
Removed 'trips' from the hardcoded resource list this workflow syncs, for the same reason -- it would otherwise report a guaranteed per-resource failure on every run.

validated_outcome: trips list: live-tested after a session refresh (the JWT expired mid-investigation, itself confirming the query reaches real auth checks) -- HTTP 200, clean empty result ([]), matching the account's genuine zero-trips state. trips list --past --upcoming and --all: both confirmed working (same clean empty result). trips get <fake-id>: confirmed reaching the real endpoint and returning a specific, correctly-surfaced domain error ('ID malformed (ID_MALFORMED)', extracted from the GraphQL response's nested extensions.exception.data.error field rather than the generic top-level 'An error occurred' message). go vet clean, full test suite passes, zero regressions. NOT YET validated: the tripDetail query's field selection against a real trip with actual flight/hotel data, since none exists in this account. If a real trip is ever available, verifying that the air/hotel field selection returns non-null, correctly-shaped data (rather than just a clean 'no trip found' for a bad ID) is the natural next step -- see .printing-press-patches/ for the full follow-up note.
